4-2-1.title: Neuron structure
4-2-1.explanation: A neuron is a specialised information-processing and information-transmitting cell. Its major structural regions are the soma (cell body), dendrites, axon and terminal buttons. Dendrites generally receive incoming information, the soma maintains the cell and integrates inputs, and the axon carries the neural message toward terminal regions.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Dendrites and axons have different typical roles.

4-2-3.title: Types of neurons
4-2-3.explanation: Neurons can be distinguished by their role in information flow. Sensory (afferent) neurons carry information toward the central nervous system, motor (efferent) neurons carry commands away from the CNS to effectors, and interneurons connect neural pathways within the CNS.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Afferent/efferent are defined relative to the CNS.

4-2-3.content_notes:
CORE IDEA
Neurons can be distinguished by their role in information flow. Sensory (afferent) neurons carry information toward the central nervous system, motor (efferent) neurons carry commands away from the CNS to effectors, and interneurons connect neural pathways within the CNS.

KEY POINTS
• sensory/afferent
• motor/efferent
• interneurons
• direction of information flow

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
Afferent means toward the CNS; efferent means away from the CNS. The distinction is about direction of information flow, not whether a neuron is physically located in the brain or spinal cord.

4-2-4.title: Neural impulse
4-2-4.explanation: Neural signalling within an axon depends on changes in membrane potential. At rest the neuron maintains a resting potential; sufficient stimulation reaches threshold and initiates an action potential. Depolarization is followed by repolarization and a refractory phase.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution
inline_nudges.text: Stimulus intensity is not coded by larger action potentials.

4-2-4.source_notes: Source-grounded synthesis from powerwithin, baron-misra, ciccarelli-white.

CORE IDEA
Neural signalling within an axon depends on changes in membrane potential. At rest the neuron maintains a resting potential; sufficient stimulation reaches threshold and initiates an action potential. Depolarization is followed by repolarization and a refractory phase.

KEY POINTS
• resting potential
• threshold
• depolarization

An action potential is not graded in amplitude: once threshold is reached, the action potential follows an all-or-none pattern. In myelinated axons, saltatory conduction makes the signal appear to jump between nodes of Ranvier.

4-2-5.title: Synaptic transmission
4-2-5.explanation: Communication between neurons occurs across a synapse rather than by direct physical continuity. An action potential reaching the axon terminal triggers processes that allow neurotransmitter substances to be released into the synaptic cleft and influence the receiving cell.

inline_nudges.label: Exam caution

CORE IDEA
Communication between neurons occurs across a synapse rather than by direct physical continuity. An action potential reaching the axon terminal triggers processes that allow neurotransmitter substances to be released into the synaptic cleft and influence the receiving cell.

KEY POINTS

DISTINCTION / CAUTION
